Opinion grounded in the ADR and stated with conditions: ADR lines 40-43 tie the choice to 1,000 shops and CH-2; lines 55-57 leave the noisy neighbor to per-shop limits (capacity plan, SLO); lines 62-64 move a shop that must be restored alone to its own database while others stay. §7 states each condition (5 shops with restore contracts; 10% promotion; restore before a bad import).

db/tenancy/row-level-security.sql line 28: "USING (shop_id = NULLIF(current_setting('app.shop_id', true), '')::integer)" — the policy compares with whatever app.shop_id the session set; it has no knowledge of the token. PG 17 5.9: rows for which the expression does not return true are not processed, so rows of the set shop pass. Settled by code inspection; Bash execution in the lab was not available in this session.

issues.text: New in round 2, in the reworded option c. The key is still correct, but the option drops the condition the lesson keeps in §8 and in q3's own explanation: an owner only "normally" skips the policy. PG 17 5.9: an owner can be made subject to it with ALTER TABLE ... FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.
issues.quote: a query run as the table's owner or a role allowed to skip the policy gets no shop condition
issues.fix: Change to "a query run as the table's owner, normally, or a role allowed to skip the policy gets no shop condition". Mirror in vi ("chủ bảng, thường là vậy,").
